sections.h2: Where Caldwell County records a deed
sections.html:
Deed records are kept in Lenoir at the Register of Deeds office, 905 West Avenue NW. Staff work the counter Monday through Friday, eight to five, and county holidays are days off.

The office has held real estate records since 1841, the year the county was formed. Filings here cover deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney and maps. Marriage licenses and birth and death records come from the same office. It does not hold wills; those belong with the Clerk of Court.

The record shows no change of owner until the buyer's deed is filed at this counter. If two claims compete, the one recorded first wins in this state, so file right after signing. The recording priority statute has the exact wording.

A standard deed of up to 15 pages is $26.00 to file, and extra pages are $4.00 apiece. Loan documents are priced higher: $64.00 for a deed of trust of up to 35 pages. One statewide schedule, G.S. 161-10, covers every county, so Lenoir sets none of these amounts itself.

Recording charges

The fee schedule is the whole fee and is collected before the document is filed. Phone ahead to find out which payment types the counter accepts.

The seller does. As grantor you pay it when the deed is lodged, and G.S. 105-228.30 assigns the duty to the transferor, to be paid to the register before filing.

  • It attaches to any instrument that conveys an interest in land.
  • Part goes to the county and part to the state.
  • The closing agent usually deducts the stamp amount from the seller's proceeds.
  • For a gift deed with no price, ask the office how it handles the stamp.

A cash sale follows the same rule. The sale price sets the amount, so agree on it with the closing attorney first.

sections.h2: What must a deed carry before the office files it?
sections.html:
Three conditions apply. Every deed must show the grantee's current mailing address. Any deed or deed of trust drawn in North Carolina must name its drafter on page one. To get the original back by mail, include a stamped envelope with your address on it.

The office scans each document when it is presented and hands it back or mails it out, so there is no waiting period for a return. The state adopted recording standards in 2002 for page layout, and the office links to them. Check them before printing, since a paper that misses the layout rules can be recorded only with the extra nonstandard fee.

Staff cannot fill in your forms or search title. You can write your own deed, but an attorney is recommended. A name can only be added to or removed from a deed by recording a new deed.

sections.h2: Searching land records before you sell
sections.html:
The register of deeds site has a free online search. Each real estate index back to the county's founding is posted there, and scanned documents go back to the early 1900s.

Look for the vesting deed, any loan still open, and any easement or road maintenance agreement on the parcel. Check for a road maintenance agreement if your driveway is shared. If your copy is gone, the office can issue a sealed certified one.

  • Spot any loan never released, then request a payoff letter.
  • Confirm that every named co-owner will sign.
  • Look for recorded agreements that run with the land.

Everything on file is public except certified vital records and recent military discharges.

sections.h2: How the tax bill affects a closing
sections.html:
If county tax is unpaid it attaches to the parcel as a lien, and the closing is where that lien gets cleared. The Tax Office shares the Lenoir address and weekday hours, and its phone is 828-757-1340. Letters to that office go to PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645.

Bills arrive in July, with a 2% early-pay discount that month and 1% in August. The due date is September 1, and the interest-free window shuts on January 5. The interest schedule in G.S. 105-360 charges 2% beginning January 6, then three-fourths of a percent each month after.

The county went through a general reappraisal for 2025, so ask the Tax Office for your parcel's current value. The same office bills the rescue readiness charge, 14 fire districts and three municipalities: Sawmills, Rhodhiss and the Village of Cedar Rock. That means one bill may carry several lines, and each line needs a payoff figure at closing. Card payments by phone go to 1-844-866-6645. The office also keeps a foreclosure list and an online listing portal for business and personal property.

sections.h2: What a seller should bring and do
sections.html:
Open the online index before closing and find your vesting deed. Check how each owner's name is spelled. Confirm that any old loan shows as released, and ask for a payoff letter if one does not. Your closing attorney drafts the deed, which must name the drafter on page one and show the buyer's mailing address.

The stamp tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing. The recording charge must be paid before the office files a thing. Enclose a prepaid, pre-addressed envelope if the original should come back by mail. After recording, the buyer appears as the owner. A cash buyer brings no new deed of trust, so usually only the deed is filed. Certified copies of the recorded deed can be ordered afterward.

If the home was inherited, wills are not kept here, so get estate paperwork from the Clerk of Court first and then record the deed that moves title. Staff cannot search title or fill in forms for you, so have your attorney or closing agent handle both. The marriage license counter closes half an hour before the rest of the office, which matters only if you are making a second errand of it.

A short order of events helps: find the vesting deed, confirm no loan is left unreleased, agree the price so the stamp amount is known, have the deed drafted, sign, and record the same day if you can. Every step before recording is yours or your attorney's, and recording is what makes the sale official in the public index.

The July 2025 population estimate is 81,105, in 38,057 housing units. Owners live in 73.5% of units, and the middle owned home value is $192,200 for 2020-2024. Median gross rent is $744.

A senior or disabled owner on a modest income can ask the Tax Office about the state exclusion. For 2026 the income ceiling is $38,800.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to file a deed with the Caldwell County register?
faqs.a: No, you can write your own deed, though an attorney is urged since staff cannot advise or search title. Whoever writes it, the deed needs the grantee's mailing address and a drafter named on page one.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Caldwell County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: You can reach the counter at 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir from eight until five, Monday to Friday. New marriage license applications stop half an hour earlier.

faqs.q: Is the stamp tax on a Caldwell County sale my cost as the seller?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. The tax is $1.00 on each $500.00 of the price, and the statute puts it on the transferor.

faqs.q: Does the Caldwell County register of deeds keep wills?
faqs.a: No. Wills are filed with the Clerk of Court. For an inherited house, take estate questions to the clerk and deed history questions here.

faqs.q: How far back do Caldwell County land records go?
faqs.a: Back to 1841, when the county was formed. Every real estate index is searchable online, and scanned images begin in the early 1900s.
